deep_analysis.name: obra/superpowers
deep_analysis.headline_hook: Superpowers transforms your coding agent from an overeager junior dev into a disciplined software architect by enforcing strict TDD, brainstorming, and subagent-driven workflows.
deep_analysis.core_functionality: Superpowers is a comprehensive software development methodology and agentic skills framework. It prevents AI coding assistants from prematurely jumping into writing code by systematically guiding them through requirement brainstorming, architectural planning, isolated git worktree setup, strict Test-Driven Development, and autonomous subagent execution loops.
key_features: Automatic skill triggering that initiates brainstorming and spec refinement sessions before any code is written.
Subagent-driven development that isolates engineering tasks across fresh subagents with continuous review loops and clean test baselines via git worktrees.
Strict RED-GREEN-REFACTOR enforcement that mandates failing tests before writing minimal implementation code.
Extensive cross-harness compatibility supporting Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Devin, GitHub Copilot, and many other CLI or app-based AI coding agents.
deep_analysis.target_audience: AI engineers, full-stack developers, and software engineering teams who heavily rely on AI coding assistants and want to eliminate hallucinated code, poor architectural design, and missing tests.
deep_analysis.practical_developer_value: Developers can use Superpowers to regain control over autonomous coding agents. Instead of dealing with messy, untested, monolithic code dumps from AI tools, developers gain a predictable, repeatable pipeline that breaks complex features into 2-5 minute bite-sized tasks, ensuring high code quality, robust test coverage, and long autonomous runtime without context drift.
suggested_use_cases: Building complex greenfield web applications with strict test coverage and architectural alignment using autonomous subagents.
Refactoring legacy codebases safely by forcing AI agents to establish clean test baselines and use isolated git worktrees.

deep_analysis.name: storytold/craft-anything
deep_analysis.headline_hook: Deconstruct any application, website, or game using a pure Rust reverse-engineering engine and have autonomous coding agents rebuild it from scratch.
deep_analysis.core_functionality: Craft Anything is an open-source, systems-level reverse-engineering and code generation engine built entirely in Rust. It systematically inspects arbitrary software, websites, or games using advanced analysis tools, then orchestrates coding agents to design, build, and iteratively verify equivalent functional implementations in a requested technology stack.
key_features: Pure Rust Reverse Engineering Engine: Features over 300 built-in native decoders, disassemblers, and decompilers that analyze codebases, binaries, web assets, and game files without relying on external runtimes.

Dual Inspection Modes (Clean Room vs. Deep): Operates strictly from observable external behavior in Clean Room mode, or unlocks comprehensive internal code and file analysis using built-in engines and Ghidra in Deep mode.

Automated Build Verification Loop: Follows a structured four-step process of Study, Build, Check, and Ready, comparing the newly generated software against original targets to iteratively correct discrepancies.

Dual Interface with Model Context Protocol (MCP) Support: Exposes its 320 capabilities uniformly across a desktop application built with egui, a command-line interface, and an MCP server so external AI agents can drive the engine directly.
deep_analysis.target_audience: Software engineers, security researchers, AI application developers, and reverse-engineering enthusiasts looking for robust automated tooling to comprehend legacy or proprietary codebases.
deep_analysis.practical_developer_value: Developers can dramatically accelerate the process of modernizing legacy software, understanding undocumented third-party libraries, or prototyping alternative implementations of existing platforms. By exposing a comprehensive CLI and MCP server, it allows developers to integrate advanced reverse-engineering and verification pipelines directly into their automated AI workflows.
suggested_use_cases: Recreating proprietary applications or web interfaces in a modern programming language or framework by studying their runtime behavior and layout.
Auditing and deconstructing native binaries, firmware, or game mechanics to generate clean-room functional equivalents and documentation.

deep_analysis.name: Verlintas/NOIR
deep_analysis.headline_hook: Transform any Android device's telemetry, permissions, and network footprint into an actionable, reproducible privacy audit report entirely offline.
deep_analysis.core_functionality: NOIR is an offline desktop utility that interfaces with Android devices via ADB to audit application manifests, runtime permissions, and hardcoded network endpoints. It computes risk scores, identifies trackers, translates permissions into real-world data exposure risks, and generates reversible remediation scripts without requiring root access or cloud telemetry.
key_features: On-device endpoint extraction using unzip and strings over ADB to minimize transfer overhead and inspect DEX-level network destinations.
Comprehensive data correlation mapping raw permissions to specific data assets like location, contacts, and media, paired with automatic manufacturer and tracker categorization.
DeepScan engine utilizing local jadx integration to perform static analysis and regex grep for high-risk runtime calls and exported components.
Automated remediation planning that outputs precise appops configurations and rollback commands for granular privacy control.
deep_analysis.target_audience: Android developers, security researchers, privacy-conscious engineers, and mobile QA specialists.
deep_analysis.practical_developer_value: Developers can use NOIR to internally audit their own Android applications for leaked network endpoints, overly permissive manifest configurations, and exposed components before shipping to production. It saves hours of manual reverse engineering by automatically orchestrating ADB pulls and static analysis workflows locally.
suggested_use_cases: Auditing pre-installed OEM apps and third-party software on personal or test Android devices for unexpected telemetry and background data leakage.
Integrating into local CI or staging workflows to verify that test builds do not contain unauthorized tracking domains or insecure debug flags.

Creating cloud infrastructure diagrams for AWS, Google Cloud, or Azure deployments directly from a textual configuration summary.
